# 0011. Build the app target in an Xcode project generated by XcodeGen

Status: Accepted

## Context

[ADR 0003](0003-fints-through-hbci4swift.md) builds FinTS on HBCI4Swift. HBCI4Swift is an Xcode framework project. It loads its syntax files from `Contents/Frameworks/HBCI4Swift.framework/Resources` inside the app bundle (`HBCISyntax.swift`, line 237), and the module map of its chip card target points into `/Applications/Xcode.app`. As a Swift package it would need changes to its code and a fork that the project keeps up to date.

[ADR 0010](0010-swift-package-and-macos-15.md) built the whole app as a Swift package because only the Command Line Tools were installed. It left an Xcode project open for later. Xcode 27.2 is now installed, and the project has an Apple Developer account. Signing with a Developer ID, notarization, string catalogs for a German interface, and an asset catalog all work directly in Xcode.

## Decision

- The libraries `Domain`, `Storage`, and `Import` stay in the Swift package at the root of the repository. `scripts/test.sh` runs their tests with the package manager.
- The app target lives in `App/`: its sources, `Info.plist`, entitlements, and resources. [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen) writes `App/MonetenMoneten.xcodeproj` from `App/project.yml`. `scripts/generate-project.sh` runs it and copies the `Package.resolved` of the package into the project, so that Xcode builds the same versions. The generated project is not in git.
- `scripts/build-app.sh` builds the app with `xcodebuild` into `dist/MonetenMoneten.app`.
- `App/Signing.xcconfig` holds the signing settings. The team ID goes into `App/Local.xcconfig`, which git ignores. Without a team, Xcode signs to run locally and leaves out the hardened runtime.
- Releases are signed with the Developer ID of the team Adanos Software GmbH. Xcode manages that certificate in the team account, so no private key leaves Apple. `scripts/build-app.sh developer-id` archives the app and exports it with this certificate. It needs an Xcode account of the team with the Admin or Account Holder role. CI will need an App Store Connect API key for the same.
- `App/project.yml` holds the version. The build number is the number of commits.
- HBCI4Swift stays unchanged in the Git submodule `Vendor/HBCI4Swift`. Its own Xcode project sets macOS 10.13, which Xcode 27 does not build, and a parent project cannot change the settings of a referenced project. So `scripts/build-hbci4swift.sh` builds `HBCI4Swift.framework` with the deployment target of the app into `.build/hbci4swift/`, and `scripts/generate-project.sh` runs it first. The Xcode project embeds that framework into `Contents/Frameworks`, where HBCI4Swift looks for its syntax files.

## Consequences

- This replaces four points of ADR 0010: the executable target `App`, the description of `scripts/build-app.sh`, "Contributors need a Mac, but not Xcode", and "HBCI4Swift must become a Swift package". Contributors need a Mac, Xcode, and XcodeGen, as [ADR 0001](0001-native-mac-app-in-swift.md) said before.
- This replaces the sentence "The app builds with `swift build`, so missing trait support in Xcode does not block this project" of [ADR 0005](0005-grdb-and-sqlcipher.md). Xcode now resolves the packages of the app, so the switch to a GRDB trait waits until Xcode supports traits.
- Xcode embeds and signs `SQLCipher.framework`. The build script no longer does that by hand.
- The unused-code check runs on the Xcode project, which builds the app and the libraries.
- If XcodeGen stops working, the generated project can be committed once and maintained in Xcode.
